confidence_notes: I ran five web searches for prices plus one for the RBA rate. Beer, coffee and the inexpensive meal are reasonably well supported. Numbeo-based figures from Expatica (June 2026) give about £20 for an inexpensive meal, £4.1 for a cappuccino and £7.1 for a 0.5L restaurant draught beer. Pub-average surveys put a London pint at about £5.8–£6.75, so I set beer between the two. Cocktail is a rough range: blog and listing sources gave about £12–£15 for a typical bar cocktail, with hotel bars much higher. I found no direct London wine-by-the-glass figure. Wine is a holistic estimate based on the UK-wide average glass price (about £5.2 in early 2025), restaurant markups of about 3x, and the local relationship to beer. Mid-range meal for two comes from my general knowledge of London restaurant prices and was not directly searched. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings. I converted GBP prices to USD using an assumed rate of about 1.32–1.33 USD per GBP that I did not verify by search, which adds some uncertainty. Prices vary widely between central and outer London.
comparable_city_reasoning: London was priced directly from aggregated UK and London price data (Numbeo-derived indexes and pub-price surveys). Accommodation anchors are based on general knowledge of London as a high-demand, high-cost Western European capital in peak summer.
